messages:
morgan_support: FYI customer (ACME) escalated — their service endpoint (svc.acme.internal) intermittently resolves to a public IP after a hosted-zone merge + cert rotation. They get NXDOMAIN then a public answer, TLS handshake fails due to wrong cert. Ticket#12345. attaching dig output they pasted.

ryan_sre: ack. do we have their repro steps? which cluster/region?

morgan_support: repro steps from customer: curl https://svc.acme.internal -> sometimes times out, sometimes connects but cert is for acme-public.example.com. region: us-west-2, cluster: acme-prod-1. They said issue started ~2026-03-12 02:00UTC right after route53 merge.

tess_network: can you paste the dig they ran? also any resolver logs?

morgan_support: pasted.

---dig paste---
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> svc.acme.internal @10.0.32.2 +short 
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
203.0.113.45

# then sometimes:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 54321

---end---

sean_eng: interesting — sounds like split-horizon: private hosted zone should answer 10.0.32.0/24 internal IP but we're seeing public IP (203.0.113.45) intermittently. That public IP is the global LB. Could be duplicate private hosted zone in another account or VPC assoc flapping.

ryan_sre: also consider node-local caches or resolver rule order. If there's a resolver rule or forwarder with higher priority that returns public answers, that could explain NXDOMAIN->public switching.

tess_network: agree. check VPC associations for duplicate private hosted zones: run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name` and inspect `VPCs` on the private zone. common gotcha after merges.

morgan_support: customer provided `dig +trace` and we see the authoritative NS flip between private nameserver and public NS for the zone.

deploybot: [auto-check] looked up hosted zones for acme.internal across accounts: found two private hosted zones: hz-1111 (acct A) assoc to vpc-abc in us-west-2, hz-2222 (acct B) assoc to vpc-def in us-west-2. Both own the same domain `acme.internal`.

sean_eng: there we go. overlapping private hosted zones with VPC associations can cause split-horizon behaviour depending on which resolver cache is hit or which VPC resolver rule is consulted. Also cert rotation might have pointed LB -> public earlier, so when public answer returned TLS mismatch occurs.

ryan_sre: remediation plan: 1) identify which hosted zone is canonical for acme.prod; 2) remove the unintended VPC association (or delete duplicate zone) in the non-canonical account; 3) force node-local DNS cache invalidation across cluster; 4) validate Route53 resolver rules for the VPC aren't forwarding to public.

tess_network: add commands to flush caches: on node-local-dns (niprod nodelocal) `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l k8s-app=node-local-dns` or if using `systemd-resolved` on EC2: `sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved`. also invalidate aws vpc resolver cache by toggling resolver rule association if needed.

morgan_support: passed steps to customer. they asked if there is a way to force Route53 immediately to stop answering public NS for the VPC.

sean_eng: only fix is to remove duplicate association / delete zone. short-term mitigate by adding a resolver rule with higher priority pointing `acme.internal` to the correct AmazonProvidedDNS in the VPC or by pinning the app to internal LB IPs (not ideal).

morgan_support: customer removed the accidental VPC association in acct B (hz-2222). after that, they still saw a few stale public answers for ~2 minutes. we asked them to restart node-local-dns pods and re-run dig.

ryan_sre: TTLs and node caches explain the residual answers. confirm after cache flush:

morgan_support: customer ran `dig @10.0.32.2 svc.acme.internal +short` -> `10.2.5.21` consistently now. TLS handshake OK. they restarted pods as advised.

sean_eng: good. root cause: overlapping private hosted zones after hosted-zone merge + cert rotation exposed public LB answers during the small window. mitigation notes: add pre-merge checklist for private zones: reconcile zone ownership, VPC associations, and run `list-hosted-zones-by-name` + cross-account lookup. also add runbook step: flush node-local caches after zone updates.

morgan_support: marking ticket 12345 resolved with root cause & steps. will follow up with customer postmortem. :white_check_mark:
